reviews.review:
For cheap, this game is well worth the price and satisfying. Good campaign although short, predictable story but satisfying fights. Enemies are weak or strong, ranged enemies in particular extremely dangerous and result in majority of my deaths. 

In short, pick it up if you enjoy shooters. Though it can at times be very repetitive.

I was interested in playing this for years, but never got around to it. I end up getting it for free last year in some promotion, but this game is sure worth buying it! At the time of the release people didn't talk too much about it and didn't sold very well either, making it something of a hidden gem these days. 

The gameplay is just a 100% straightforward fun action with no bulls**t and it plays great with a Xbox controller (which makes a lot easier to switch from melee to gun-action). The game have good graphics for the time and a very good art direction (even if it still kinda follows the monochromatic rules of the "brown years of gaming", which started with Gears of Wars), it also runs completely smooth, I didn't get any bugs (except for a single servo-skull which didn't registered as picked up even after I played the message) or crashes through the whole game. 

I will make a little speculation here and say there is a lot of similarities between this and DOOM 2016, like the finishes (especially the chainsaw ones, that even predates Brutal Doom) which is the only way to replenish life, the no bulls***t straightforward arena-like gameplay and even [spoiler]the plot of a crazy scientist who uses some hellish dimension as an energy source, but end up releasing demons on the planet. This is different from the plot of previous Doom games, which were about teleportation going wrong and ancient artifacts[/spoiler].  And the whole vibe of this game is quite similar to DOOM 2016 and very different of the "cover-hiding/regenerating-health" shooters of it time. if this was actually an inspiration, it was a very appropriated one for bringing back Doom for modern times.

I can say this is a nearly perfect game for what it's trying to accomplish [spoiler](it was not perfect only because you don't drive the Titan and that silly quick-time event at the end)[/spoiler], it's a shame that we'll probably never get a sequel.

If you want to live the ultimate male power fantasy then this is the game for you. In this game you play Captain Titus, a mountain of flesh and steel that turns orks into a cloud of red mist with his massive chainsaw sword. The story is incredibly straight forward and basically just points you towards hordes of enemies you need to pulverize. The voice acting is amazing and dialogue is brief, but still gives you all the information you need to understand what is happening. Still holds up in 2019 and I cant wait to finish the game.

Probably the worst Warhammer 40k game for me.
The gameplay is really shallow, game world closed and extremely linear, and the story sucks.
This can not even compare to other 40k games. Its just that bad.
I tried it multiple times, over a few months. No a single time could i play in more then 1h. It just not interesting.
There is no skill or brain involved, just aim with an oversized reticle and smash the melee button, while using executions to heal in-between.
I am a big fan of 40k series, but this game is just a pile of trash. Skip it.
2/10
